items.headline: DXY closes 102.33 (+0.73%) — biggest daily gain in nearly five months as the +165K payrolls beat re-arms the Dec Fed hike (~77%, CME FedWatch)
UoM sentiment beats (51.0 vs 48.1), inflation expectations cool to 4.3% — the dollar holds its payrolls gains
Ueda: real rates 'have not risen significantly' — no pushback on the ~80% December BoJ hike
Lane: ECB to 'gather information between now and December'; EZ retail sales miss (-0.7% m/m, biggest fall since June 2024), German IP beats (+0.7% on autos)
Oil gives back the morning spike: Brent ~$97.8, WTI ~$90.2 at the close; spot gold ~$4,051 as the dollar jumps

items.headline: Nov 3 CFTC cut released 2:30pm CT — percentile scoring carries to the 2am run; board scores still on the Oct 27 cut
Next test: US Oct CPI Tue Nov 10; RBA decision lands Mon evening CT (Dec 7-8 meeting)
US payrolls BEAT +165K in October (vs 65K fcst); unemployment 4.1%, wages +0.4% m/m — DXY jumps to 102.20 (+0.62%); Dec Fed hike case re-armed
Canada jobs MISS: employment -4.7K (vs +14.6K fcst), unemployment 6.7% (from 6.5%) — USD/CAD ~1.4100; BoC Dec hike case questioned
Dollar gathers strength toward 102.00 in London ahead of payrolls; EUR/USD ~1.118, GBP/USD ~1.340, USD/JPY ~158.0, AUD weakest again (~0.688)
US futures try a mild bounce into London; Dec Fed hike ~70% into payrolls (vs ~68% Asia); Brent ~$99.96, gold ~$4,052
AI rout spreads to Asia: Nasdaq -5.5% Thursday (steepest since April 2025) on data-center scrutiny fears; Asia tech crumbles Friday
Dollar firms in Asia (DXY ~101.7) as haven flows lift yen to one-week high 157.27; 10Y 4.84%, 2Y 4.47%
Oil up a second day in Asia: Brent ~$99.9 (+1.6%), WTI ~$91.6 (+1.2%) on Hormuz supply worries; still set for ~12% weekly drop
Gold eases to ~$4,063 (-0.6%) as oil rebound fans inflation worries; Dec Fed hike 68% (CME FedWatch)
Eurasia cuts Iran-deal odds to 10% (from 20%), US-attack odds to 60% (from 65%) as Tehran's proposal via Qatar is reviewed

NY close: dollar flat (DXY ~101.4, little changed) but Aussie weakest and yen strongest — AUD/USD 0.6935 (-1.02%), USD/JPY 157.82 (-0.38%) — as a tech/chip-led US equity selloff drives haven flows; EUR/USD $1.1225, GBP/USD $1.3467, USD/CHF 0.8158, USD/CAD 1.3989, NZD/USD 0.5597

Oil rebounds after Wednesday's ~9% crash: Brent $97.94 (+3.5%) and WTI $90.64 (+2.8%) as traders reassess the Iran war — Eurasia Group cuts deal odds to 10% (from 20%), renewed US strikes 60%; two tankers and a tug caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; JPMorgan: global market back in surplus (1.4M bpd Oct)
